# 2-Week Intro Statistics Exam Plan

A focused 14-day plan for **90 minutes per day**, built around your biggest pain points: **probability, hypothesis testing, and p-values**. It uses spaced review so earlier topics come back several times before the exam on **2026-04-20**.

## Daily Study Roadmap

| Day | Focus | Key Tasks | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Foundations + setup | Review course outline; diagnostic quiz; list formulas; make error log | Identify weak spots and organize materials |
| Day 2 | Descriptive statistics | Mean, median, SD, variance; interpret graphs; 10 practice questions | Get fast with core summary stats |
| Day 3 | Probability basics | Sample spaces, events, complements, conditional probability | Build probability vocabulary and setup |
| Day 4 | Probability practice | Independent vs dependent events; Bayes basics if covered; mixed drills | Improve accuracy on probability problems |
| Day 5 | Random variables + distributions | Discrete vs continuous; expected value; normal/binomial basics | Connect probability to distributions |
| Day 6 | Spaced review 1 | 30 min probability review; 30 min stats review; 30 min mixed quiz | Reinforce Days 2–5 |
| Day 7 | Sampling + standard error | Sampling distributions, CLT, standard error, z-scores | Understand how samples behave |
| Day 8 | Hypothesis testing basics | Null/alternative, test statistics, critical values, test flow | Learn the full test procedure |
| Day 9 | p-values + interpretation | What p-value means; common mistakes; decision rules; practice wording | Fix the most important concept gap |
| Day 10 | Hypothesis testing practice | One-sample z/t tests if covered; two-sided vs one-sided; mixed problems | Build procedural confidence |
| Day 11 | Confidence intervals + link to tests | Confidence intervals, margin of error, relation to significance tests | Strengthen interpretation and connection |
| Day 12 | Spaced review 2 | 30 min probability; 30 min hypothesis testing; 30 min p-values drill | Second retrieval pass on weak areas |
| Day 13 | Full mixed review | Mixed set across all topics; redo missed questions; formula recall | Close remaining gaps |
| Day 14 | Final mock-exam session | 2-hour mock exam + targeted revision priorities | Simulate exam and lock in readiness |

## Daily Task Breakdown

### Day 1: Diagnostic and Study Setup
- Take a short diagnostic quiz covering all major topics.
- Mark every missed question by topic.
- Build a one-page formula sheet.
- Start an error log with columns: topic, mistake, correct idea.

### Day 2: Descriptive Statistics
- Review mean, median, mode, variance, and standard deviation.
- Practice reading histograms, boxplots, and scatterplots.
- Do 10 short problems with interpretation.
- End by summarizing when each statistic is most useful.

### Day 3: Probability Foundations
- Review sample spaces, events, and complements.
- Practice probability notation and tree diagrams.
- Work 6–8 conditional probability questions.
- Write out the difference between “and,” “or,” and “given.”

### Day 4: Probability Drill Day
- Do mixed probability problems without notes.
- Focus on independence vs dependence.
- If Bayes’ rule is in your course, do 2–3 problems.
Media: Alt=If Bayes’ rule is in your course, do 2–3 problems, An Introductory Statistics Exam
- Revisit every missed question from Day 3.

### Day 5: Random Variables and Distributions
- Review discrete vs continuous variables.
- Study expected value and variance conceptually.
- Practice binomial and normal distribution questions if included.
- Connect distribution shape to probability questions.

### Day 6: Spaced Review 1
- 30 minutes: probability review from Days 3–5.
- 30 minutes: descriptive statistics review.
- 30 minutes: mixed quiz.
- Update the error log with repeated mistakes.

### Day 7: Sampling and Standard Error
- Review sampling distributions and the central limit idea.
- Practice z-scores and standard error calculations.
- Focus on what changes when sample size changes.
- Do 5–7 problems that combine sampling and interpretation.

### Day 8: Hypothesis Testing Basics
- Learn the full test sequence:
  - state hypotheses
  - choose significance level
  - compute test statistic
  - compare with cutoff or p-value
  - conclude in context
- Practice identifying null and alternative hypotheses.
- Do a few “what is the correct conclusion?” questions.

### Day 9: p-values and Interpretation
- Write a plain-language definition of p-value.
- Practice translating p-values into decisions.
- Drill common traps:
  - p-value is not the probability the null is true
  - p-value is not the probability results happened by chance alone
- Do 8–10 interpretation questions.

### Day 10: Hypothesis Testing Practice
- Solve mixed testing problems from start to finish.
- Compare one-sided and two-sided tests.
- Practice matching p-values to decisions at different alpha levels.
- Rework every missed p-value question from Day 9.

### Day 11: Confidence Intervals and Connections
- Review how confidence intervals relate to hypothesis tests.
- Practice interpreting intervals in context.
- Compare interval width, sample size, and variability.
- Do a mixed set of 6–8 questions.

### Day 12: Spaced Review 2
- 30 minutes: probability.
- 30 minutes: hypothesis testing.
- 30 minutes: p-values and confidence intervals.
- Focus only on error-log topics and questions you previously missed.

### Day 13: Full Mixed Review
- Do a mixed practice set across all topics.
- Redo the hardest questions without looking at solutions first.
- Recite key definitions and formulas from memory.
- Prepare your final exam-day formula sheet.

### Day 14: Final 2-Hour Mock-Exam Session
- 90 minutes: full timed mock exam under realistic conditions.
- 30 minutes: review mistakes and revise only the highest-value topics.

### Revision Priorities for the Final 30 Minutes
- **Probability:** conditional probability, independence, complements, tree diagrams
- **Hypothesis testing:** null/alternative, test steps, decision rules
- **p-values:** interpretation in words, common misconceptions, decision-making
- **Confidence intervals:** how they connect to significance tests
- **Error log:** redo the 3 most frequent mistake types
